name: Wildflower seeds
description: A mix of small meadow-flower seeds. Quick to sprout in open, sunny ground.

facts.text: Mature wildflowers drop fresh seed, so one patch can become many.

name: Moss spores
description: Fine dust gathered from established moss. Settles best on damp, shaded ground.

facts.text: Moss has no seeds or flowers; it spreads by spores and fragments.

name: Fern spores
description: Spores shed from the undersides of mature fern fronds.

facts.text: Fern spores need moisture to grow into new ferns.

name: Grass seeds
description: Seed heads from ornamental grasses. Hardy and unfussy.

name: Maple samaras
description: Winged maple seeds that spin as they fall. Patience turns one into a tree.

facts.text: The paired wings of a samara slow its fall so the wind can carry it.

name: Rush cuttings
description: Young shoots of soft rush, ready to settle into wet ground at the pond's edge.

name: Twigs
description: Small fallen branches. The backbone of most natural shelters.

facts.text: Old trees and overgrown corners are the best places to find twigs.

name: Bark
description: Loose strips of bark shed by old trees. Good for roofing a shelter.

facts.text: Many beetles shelter under loose bark.

name: Stones
description: Weathered garden stones, some still carrying patches of moss.

facts.text: Stone arrangements give small creatures cool, sheltered crevices.

name: Leaf litter
description: Fallen leaves and needles. Keeps a shelter damp and snug.

facts.text: Leaf litter slowly breaks down into rich soil.

name: Bamboo shoots
description: Young shoots lifted from the edge of a bamboo clump, ready to start a new one.

facts.text: New bamboo culms reach their full height in a single season.

name: Bamboo canes
description: Light, strong, hollow canes cut from mature bamboo.

facts.text: Hollow canes make ideal nesting tubes for solitary bees.

name: Forest grass divisions
description: Small clumps split from Japanese forest grass, each ready to root.

facts.text: Forest grass spreads slowly by short underground stems.

name: Hosta divisions
description: A crown of hosta, divided with its roots, waiting for a shady spot.

facts.text: Hostas are grown for their leaves, but their tall flower spikes feed bees.

name: Maple leaves
description: Fine, deeply cut leaves from a mature Japanese maple, glowing red and orange.

facts.text: Fallen leaves make soft, insulating nest linings.

hints.text: A fully grown maple may yield something new.

name: Maple sap
description: A little clear, faintly sweet sap that weeps from a mature maple.

facts.text: Some butterflies, like the red admiral, feed on tree sap as well as nectar.

hints.text: A fully grown maple may yield something new.

name: Seed bundle
description: Spare seeds wrapped in leaves and tied with grass: a store of food that draws insects and birds to a shelter.

facts.text: Seed heads left standing feed birds and shelter insects through the lean months.

name: Water lily rhizomes
description: A knobbly root of water lily, ready to sink into pond mud.

facts.text: Water lilies root in the mud and send their leaves up to the surface.

name: Reed rhizomes
description: A length of creeping reed root with a fresh shoot.

facts.text: Reeds spread along the margin by creeping roots.

name: Hornwort sprigs
description: Feathery sprigs of a pond plant that lives wholly under water.

facts.text: Hornwort has no roots; it drifts in deeper water.

name: Reed stems
description: Dry, hollow reed stems, light and easy to weave.

facts.text: Bundled reed stems make shelters and screens.

hints.text: Mature reeds shed stems you can gather.

name: Clay
description: Smooth grey clay from the pond banks.

facts.text: Clay holds water, which is why the old pond still has its shape.

hints.text: Clearing the overgrown banks may turn up clay.

name: Lichen fragments
description: Crusty flakes of lichen that will take hold on bare stone.

facts.text: A lichen is a fungus and an alga living as one.

name: Thyme cuttings
description: Fragrant sprigs of creeping thyme, ready to root.

facts.text: Thyme roots easily from a sprig pressed into dry soil.

name: Fescue seeds
description: Fine seeds of a tough blue-grey grass.

facts.text: Fescues thrive where the soil is thin and dry.

name: Dwarf pine seedling
description: A tiny pine in a ball of gritty soil.

facts.text: Dwarf pines grow only a few centimetres a year.

name: Gravel
description: Pale, rounded gravel from the old stone garden.

facts.text: Raked gravel stands for water in many Japanese dry gardens.

hints.text: Clearing the stone garden’s overgrowth turns up gravel.

name: River stones
description: Smooth, water-worn stones, grey and speckled.

facts.text: Stones warm in the sun and hold the heat into the evening.

hints.text: Old river stones lie hidden under the stone garden’s overgrowth.

name: Royal fern spores
description: Green spores from the tip of a royal fern frond.

facts.text: Royal ferns carry their spores on special upright fronds.

name: Wood sorrel seeds
description: Tiny seeds that pop from wood sorrel’s pods.

facts.text: The ripe pods flick their seeds a surprising distance.

name: Mushroom spawn
description: Threads of fungus in a handful of damp sawdust.

facts.text: A mushroom is only the fruit; the fungus lives as threads in the wood.

name: Deadwood
description: Old, softening branches from the woodland floor.

facts.text: Decaying wood is home to more life than living wood.

hints.text: Fallen wood lies hidden under the hollow’s overgrowth.

name: Leaf mould
description: Dark, crumbly earth made from rotted leaves.

facts.text: Leaf mould holds water like a sponge and feeds the soil.

hints.text: Leaf litter left to rot in a bed becomes rich leaf mould.

name: Clover seeds
description: Tiny kidney-shaped seeds of white clover.

facts.text: Clover enriches poor soil as it grows.

name: Oxeye daisy seeds
description: Fine dark seeds from a dried daisy head.

facts.text: One daisy head holds hundreds of seeds.

name: Aster seeds
description: Light, tufted seeds of a late-flowering aster.

facts.text: Aster seeds drift away on little parachutes.

name: Bellflower seeds
description: Dust-fine seeds shaken from a bellflower pod.

facts.text: Bellflower seeds need light to sprout.

name: Meadow grass seeds
description: A mix of tall meadow grass seed.

facts.text: Tall grasses give meadow insects shelter.

name: Seed heads
description: Dry flower heads full of ripe seed.

facts.text: Left standing, seed heads feed birds through the winter.

hints.text: Meadow flowers shed seed heads once they have flowered.

name: Grass stems
description: Long, dry meadow grass stems.

facts.text: Dry grass stems are used to thatch and to weave.

hints.text: Tall meadow grass sheds dry stems.
